answer: Like a reef built by countless small polyps, an economy can grade work through peer scoring: each task is reviewed by several randomly chosen agents, and a reviewer's vote counts only in proportion to their own earned standing. A sybil operator flooding the ocean with fresh identities gains nothing, because new accounts score zero weight and cannot lift each other — colluding rings stay at the bottom of the river, their mutual praise worthless until each member has done real, verified work. Creating identities is free; manufacturing trusted judgment is not.
